context: Parallel coordinates chart for 150 synthetic cities across 6 metrics (population, temp, elevation, rainfall, GDP, density), with a linked sparkline histogram table that updates on brush filter
first_impression: Structurally sound parallel coordinates with data-driven y-scales and a well-anchored sparkline table, but sparkline y-axes silently rescale on filter creating frequency distortion.
what_works: Y-scales use d3.extent(data) anchored to the full dataset so brushing doesn't cause axis jumping; sparkline histogram bars have a proper zero baseline with domain [0, d3.max(bins, b => b.length)].
what_doesnt: Sparkline sy domain recalculates from the filtered subset's max bin count on every brush update, so 10 selected cities fill the same bar height as 150, masking the true frequency drop; nBins is hardcoded at 30 regardless of subset size (Sturges' rule would give ~8 bins for n=150).
